entities.text: JUDGMENT Parmila P vs Narasimha Reddy
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 1 The petitioner has filed this petition U/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by her in a road traffic accident that occurred on 09-04-2024.

2. The petition averments in brief are as under:
On 09-04-2024 at about 9.00 a.m., the petitioner was proceeding as a pillion rider in two wheeler bearing Reg.No. KA.64.W.1950 near Domathamari village, Hindupura road, Kasaba hobli, Pavagada taluk, Tumakuru, which was ridden by its rider in a rash and negligent manner without observing traffic rules, at the same time a dog came across the bike and ride applied brake suddenly, due to the said impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.
Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to Pavagada Government hospital wherein first aid treatment has been provided.

Further petitioner has been shifted to Bangalore BJS Hospital, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient and also underwent surgery for which he has spent Rs.10,00,000/- towards treatment,
medicines, conveyance, nourishing food and other incidental charges etc.,
Prior to the accident, petitioner was very hale and healthy, aged about 38 years and working at Private and thereby earning Rs.30,000/- per month.
Due to the accidental injuries petitioner is not able to do any work.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle,
are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, prays to award compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- with interest.
3. In spite of service of notice, respondent No.1- owner has not appeared before the court, hence, he has been placed exparte.
After service of notice, respondent No.2 -insurer appeared through its counsel and filed written statement.

The respondent No.2 insurance company has filed objection statement by admitting the issuance of policy to the offending two wheeler bearing No.KA-64-W-1950 and the liability of this respondent if any, is subject to the terms and condition of the insurance policy.
It is contended that, the rider of the motorcycle was riding the vehicle without having DL.
Further it is submitted to permit this respondent to contest the above matter on all the grounds available under Sec.170 of MV Act.

It is contended that due to the negligence and carelessness of the rider of the two wheeler the pillion rider/petitioner might have been sustained some minor injuries and petitioner in collusion with the local police has falsely implicated the two wheeler by lodging frivolous complaint against the rider of the two-wheeler after a lapse of 5 days.
Further denied the age, avocation and income of the petitioner.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive, exorbitant, imaginary and baseless.
Hence, the respondent No.2 insurance company prays to dismiss the petition against it.

Parmila P vs Narasimha Reddy on 10 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117387638/
2 4.

On the basis of the rival contention, the following issues are framed by this court:
1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries due to the actionable negligent riding of motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-64-W-6833 by its rider, in RTA took place on 09.04.2024 at about 9.00 a.m. near Domathamari village, Hindupura road, Kasaba Hobli, Pava- gada Taluk, Tumkuru?
2. Whether the petitioner is enti- tled for compensation?
If so, what amount and from whom?

3 . What Order or Award?
5.
In order to prove the claim petition, the petitioner examined herself as P.W.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.1 to 11.

Further, examined four witnesses as PW.2 to 5, through them got marked documents at Ex.P.12 to 36.
6.
Heard the arguments of both sides and perused the material evidence that are available on record.
7. My findings on the above issues are as under.

Issue No.1 : In the affirmative;
 Issue No.2 : In the affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per final orders  for the following:-
 : R E A S O N S:
 ISSUE NO.1 :
8.
That by reiterating all the averments made in the petition, the petitioner has filed her affidavit in lieu of- examination in-chief, which is considered as P.W.1.
In support of her case, she has produced true copies of FIR, complaint, spot mahazar, IMV report, wound certificate, IMV report, charge sheet, which are marked under Ex.P.1 to P.5 and P.8 .
9. On perusal of Ex.P1- FIR which is registered on the basis of Ex.P2 first information given by one Adhilakshmamma who is the mother of petitioner.
After the registration of FIR as per Ex.P1, the Ex.P3 spot mahazar was prepared by the I.O.
On perusal of the contents of mahazar, at the time of spot inspection the IO has found blood stains in the accident spot.
At the time of conducting spot mahazar the IO has also seized the offending motorcycle in the accident spot.
10. The Ex.P5 IMV report wherein it is noted that no fresh damages found at the time of inspection of vehicle/ Two-wheeler bearing No.KA-64-W-1950.

It is the contention of the petitioner that when Parmila P vs Narasimha Reddy on 10 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117387638/
3 she was traveling as a pillion rider the rider of the motorcycle applied sudden brake due to which the petitioner fell down.

entities.text: Parmila P vs Narasimha Reddy on 10 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thereby as the petitioner herself fell on the road due to the sudden brake applying of the rider no damages can be expected on the offending motorcycle.

11. By filing the written statement the respondent No.2 insurance company has taken major defence by denying the involvement of Two-wheeler bearing No.KA- 64-W-1950 in the accident and also the complaint is given after 5 days by falsely implicating Two-wheeler bearing No.KA-64-W-1950 in the accident.

12. In this regard if we perused the Ex.P14 & P15 MLC and police intimation, in the Ex.P14 MLC register extract the reason for the injuries sustained by the petitioner is noted as alleged history of RTA from 2 wheeler, while patient is a pillion rider.
In the Ex.P15 police intimation it is shown as the petitioner admitted to their hospital for treatment with alleged history of RTA fall from 2 wheeler .
The Ex.P14 & P15 both of dated 09.04.2024.

On the date of accident itself the hospital authorities have issued police intimation as per Ex.P15, as such even though there is a delay of 5 days in registering the FIR can be over looked by saying that the MLC and police intimation was duly prepared on 09-04- 2024 by intimating the police about the accident dated 09-04-2024.

Thus the fact of the accident is established by producing the Ex.P14 & P15.
13.

The learned counsel for the respondent No.2 vehemently argues that there is an inordinate delay of 5 days in lodging the FIR and the same cannot be brushed aside lightly, instead has to be construed as a circumstance showing that the case is an afterthought and the offending vehicle is implicated in the case even though it is not involved in the accident.
But not every delay would move this court to view the case of the petitioners doubtfully.
Because there might be genuine circumstances that could have contributed to the delay.
In fact only if the delay is left unexplained the same needs to be viewed seriously.

No doubt in the facts of this case, the accident occurred on 09-04-2024 at about 8.30 p.m, but the FIR was lodged on 13-04-2024 at about 11.00 a.m., and hence it is evident that the FIR is lodged after 5 days of occurrence of the accident.

But the informant in the Ex.P2 first information it is stated that soon after the accident the petitioner was shifted to hospital and underwent with treatment as such, they were unable to give the complaint immediately.

Along with this the petitioner also examined Medical Records incharge at Gleneagles BGS Hospital as PW2 and he has produced Ex.P14 & 15 MLC register extract and Police intimation wherein it is stated that alleged history of RTA from 2 wheeler, while patient is a pillion rider.
14. The respondent No.1 owner of the offending two- wheeler has not appeared before the court.
The respondent No.2-insurance comapny has not denied the fact of accident but only the fact of negligence and liability is disputed.

15. Further the wound certificate marked at Ex.P4 and discharge summary marked at Ex.P9 also discloses that on the date of accident itself the petitioner was admitted to their hospital with a history of RTA.
The endeavor of the injured usually will be getting the treatment to the injured than thinking about the legal formalities.

Parmila P vs Narasimha Reddy on 10 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117387638/
4

Perhaps the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Ravi v. Badrinarayan and others reported in AIR 2011 SC 1226, has observed thus:
"The purpose of lodging the FIR in motor accident cases is primarily to intimate the police to initiate investigation of criminal offences.

entities.text: Ravi v. Badrinarayan and others reported in AIR 2011 SC 1226
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Lodging of FIR certainly proves factum of accident so that the victim is able to lodge a case for compensation but delay in doing so cannot be the main ground for rejecting the claim petition.

In other words, although lodging of FIR is vital in deciding motor accident claim cases, delay in lodging the same should not be treated as fatal for such proceedings, if claimant has been able to demonstrate satisfactory and cogent reasons for it.
There could be variety of reasons in genuine cases for delayed lodgment of FIR.
Unless kith and kin of the victim are able to regain a certain level of tranquillity of mind and are composed to lodge it, even if there is delay, the same deserve to be condoned.
In such circumstances, the authenticity of the FIR assumes much more significance than delay in lodging thereof supported by cogent reasons.

If the court finds that there is no indication of fabrication or it has not been concocted or engineered to implicate innocent persons then even if there is a delay in lodging the FIR, the claim case cannot be dismissed merely on that ground."
(Emphasis supplied by me) Hence the delay of 5 days, in the light of reasons assigned by the PW.1 and also as mentioned in the Ex.P2, complaint, Ex.P14 - MLC, Ex.P15- police intimation and Ex.P4 wound certificate and Ex.P9 discharge summary it cannot be considered as inordinate.
16.

Further on perusal of the contents of Ex.P3 & 5 spot mahazar and IMV report, the petitioner successfully established the negligence of rider of motor cycle bearing No. KA-64-W-1950 and thereby no reasons are made out to consider the contributory negligence by the petitioner as the petitioner is a pillion rider.
17. Ex

. P8 charge sheet is filed against the rider of the Two-wheeler bearing No.KA-64-W-1950, the IO has opined that the negligence is on the part of driver of the offending Two-wheeler bearing No.KA-64-W-1950.
18.

In a claim for compensation under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319 Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others.

entities.text: 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319 Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 19. Further the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others (2009) 13 SCC 530, wherein it is held that, it was necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.

entities.text: Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others (2009) 13 SCC 530
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The claimants were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.

In this context by considering the contents of Ex.P1 to 8 this court tilts in Parmila P vs Narasimha Reddy on 10 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117387638/
5 favour of the petitioner as the petitioner has to prove the alleged negligence on the basis of the evidence and proof of the same on preponderance of probabilities.
20. As per well settled principle of law, the standard of proof in the claim petition like the present is preponderance of the probability.
There are no grounds to disbelieve the case of petitioner in the absence of rebuttal evidence.

All the materials available on record leading to show that, petitioner has sustained injuries in the accident took place on 09-04-2024 which is caused by the rider of the motor cycle bearing No.KA-64-W-1950 which belongs to respondent No.1 and insured with respondent No.2.
There is no reason to discard the evidence of petitioner.
In the claim petition like present one strict proof is not necessary, but preponderance of probabilities is sufficient.
Accordingly, issue No.1 answered in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.2:
21.
As already held herein above, the petitioner has proved that she has sustained injuries in RTA which is caused by respondent No.1.
Hence, the petitioner is entitle for compensation.
Now the quantum of compensation is to be ascertained on different heads.

The petitioner examined MRO of Gleneagles BGS Hospital as PW.2 and got marked documents at Ex.P12 to 17.
a) PAIN AND AGONY:-
At the time of alleged accident the petitioner was aged about 38 years.
Aadhaar card produced at Ex.P11 shows the date of birth of the petitioner as 01.01.1986, the accident was occurred on 09.04.2024, as on the date of accident petitioner was aged about 38 years.
In the petition itself she has averred that immediately after the accident she was shifted to Gleneagles BGS Hospital wherein she was admitted as inpatient.

As per the discharge summary marked at Ex.P9 the petitioner was an inpatient from 09.04.2024 to 25.04.2024 and sustained severe traumatic brain injury, diffuse axonal injury, comminuted mildly displaced fracture of left,
supraorbital margin, left radial styloid undisplaced fracture and fracture of right distal phalynx great toe.
By considering the nature of the injuries and period she spent to overcome the pain and other allied effects of the accident Rs.80,000/- may be awarded to the petitioner under this head.
b) Medical expenses:
The petitioner has produced medical bills as per Ex.P10, amounting to Rs.5,63,428/-.
In the cross-examination petitioner denied the suggestion that he has not spent Rs.15,00,000/- towards treatment and all the medical expenses borne by Bajaj Health Insurance.

Petitioner has also examined Billing department Senior Executive at Gleneagles BGS Hospital as PW3 and he has produced Delivery order, inpatient final bill along with break up bill, receipts,
inpatient advance receipts, 9 inpatient receipts duplicate copies at Ex.P19 to P.23.
As per PW3 and the documents produced by the PW3 the petitioner has obtained loan to pay the medical bills and no reimbursement was done to the petitioner from any Health Insurance plans.
As per Ex.P.20 they have mentioned as Bajaj Finserv Health Limited which is given loan to the petitioner.

The delivery note of the Bajaj Finance Limited as per Ex.P.19 is also produced which shows that the petitioner Parmila P vs Narasimha Reddy on 10 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117387638/
6 borrowed loan from Bajaj Finance to pay the medical bills.
These bills are supported by the prescriptions marked at Ex.P.10.
The case sheet marked at Ex.P17 also supported the bills produced by the petitioner.
No grounds are made out to disbelieving these bills.
Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case in combined with the alleged injuries the petitioner is entitled for the reimbursement of the same by rounding of the same i.e., Rs.5,63,500/-.
c) Loss of income during laid up period: The petitioner has stated that he was working at Private and earning Rs.30,000/- p.m.
In this regard petitioner has not produced any documents.
Such being the case, it is just and necessary to consider the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.16,500/- p.m. as the accident is of the year 2024.
As per the discharge summary marked at Ex.P9 the petitioner was admitted to Gleneagles BGS Hospital for a period of 17 days.

Thereafter usually the healing period has to be considered for which in the absence of evidence, this court is of the opinion that in total four months period including 17 days inpatient period may be considered under this head as a loss of income.
So, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.16,500 X 4 months = Rs.66,000/- during the laid up period.

d) Disability;- To prove the nature of injuries sustained by him the petitioner has examined Dr.Shailesh A.V. Rao, Neurosurgeon at Padmashree Diagnostics, Bengaluru as PW.5, through him OPD records, neuro psychological assessment report and MMSE report are marked at Ex.P34 to Ex.P.36.
According to the evidence of this witness the petitioner sustained head injury.
He examined the petitioner for assessment of disability.
Petitioner suffered neuro psychological disability of 40-70% and permanent disability to whole body at 20%.
On clinical observation, the PW.5 found that the petitioner has not been able to attend the earlier work as a tailor in a private garments company.
Petitioner complains of frequent headaches, giddiness and impaired memory.
Further PW5 found that conscious ambulant patient with impaired memory, petitioner had weakness of left upper limb.
The PW.5 doctor is cross-examined at length by the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 insurance company.
No doubt that the PW.5 is not a treated doctor but assessed the disability of neurological assessment by using DGHS guidelines of Indian Phsyciatric association.
Nothing been elicited to disbelieve the case of the petitioner at the time of cross examination of PW.5.
But when the petitioner can answer the fact of accident in a proper and accurate way, whether the evidence of Pw.5 regarding the cognitive disability can be considered or not has to be looked into.
No doubt that the petitioner's normal life is disturbed by the accident.
But as per the evidence of PW.5 doctor in the complex situation the petitioner cannot behave normally.
As per the PW.5 the petitioner behaves normal in the simple comprehensive situation.
But in the complex situations the condition of the petitioner is impaired.
By considering the same, for a person to lead his life in a normal way without depending on others, they have to behave and react normally in both normal and complex situation.
The total body disability disability of the petitioner is assessed at 20%.
It is stated that the petitioner was working at Private but no evidence is placed in this regard.
By considering the nature of the work of the petitioner certainly the disability caused by the injuries sustained in the accident it may effect the working capacity of the petitioner.

Hence the functional disability of the petitioner by Parmila P vs Narasimha Reddy on 10 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117387638/
7 considering the alleged nature of work is assessed at 18%.
The petitioner has produced his Aadhar card marked at Ex.P11, as per this document the year of birth of the petitioner is shown as 01.01.1986.
The accident was occurred in the year-2024.
So, as on the date of the accident the petitioner was aged 38 years.
As per Sarala Verma's case, the proper multiplier applicable to the age of petitioner is '15'.
Hence, I inclined to award future loss of income at Rs.16,500/- X 12 X 15 X 18% =Rs.5,34,600/- which is the total loss of future income.
e) FOOD, NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE;
As per Ex.P9 discharge summary, the petitioner took treatment as inpatient for a period of 17 days.
As per wound certificate marked at Ex.P4 the injuries sustained by the petitioner are grievous in nature.

By considering the nature of the injuries and period he spent to overcome the pain and other allied effects of the accident he is entitled for compensation of Rs.50,000/- towards food and nourishment, conveyance.
f) ATTENDANT CHARGES:
The petitioner sustained grievous injuries in the accident.
The petitioner has spent 17 days in the hospital and there is no evidence or pleading in this regard to show that the petitioner is in need of attendant.

But by considering the nature of the fracture as discussed above, it may be considered to award attendant charges at Rs.1,000/- per day i.e.,
Rs.17,000/- in total as the petitioner has spent 17 days in the hospital.
g) Towards loss of amenities and enjoyment of life:
The petitioner admitted to the hospitals for the injuries sustained by her, which might certainly have deprived her of the basic comforts and enjoyment.
Therefore, it is just and proper to award a reasonable sum of Rs.50,000/- under this head.
h) Future Medical Expenses:
No evidence is available to show that the petitioner is need of future medical assistance or future surgery for removal of implant.
In the absence of evidence the petitioner is not entitled for any compensation under this head.

Thus, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
a. Towards pain and agony Rs. 80,000/-
b. Towards medical expenses Rs. 5,63,500/- c. Towards loss of income during Rs.
66,000/-
laid up period d.
Towards disability Rs. 5,34,600/-
e. Towards food, nourishment and Rs. 50,000/-
Parmila

8 conveyance f.
Towards attendant charges Rs. 17,000/- g.

Towards loss of amenities Rs. 50,000/-
Total Rs.13,61,100/-
22. Liability:- According to the petitioner the respondent No.1 & 2 are the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle.
The respondent No.2 in its objection statement has admitted the issuance of policy to the Two wheeler bearing No.KA-64-W-1950 and the policy was in force at the time of accident.
No other grounds are made out by showing the violation of policy condition by the respondent No.1.

Hence, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner and the respondent No.2 insurance company shall indemnify the compensation on behalf of the respondent No.1.
The petitioner is entitle for compensation with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,
Accordingly, this issue answered partly in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.3:
23.

For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.13,61,100/- (Rupees Thirteen lakh sixty one thousand one hundred only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till the realization from respondents.
The respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.

Out of total compensation amount awarded to the Petitioner, 75% of the same to be released in favour of petitioner through E-payment on her proper identification and remaining 25% to be kept in Fixed Deposit in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank, for a period of three years, in her name.
Advocate fee is fixed at 1,500/-.
Draw up award accordingly.

Because there might be genuine circumstances that could have contributed to the delay.
In fact only if the delay is left unexplained the same needs to be viewed seriously.
No doubt in the facts of this case, the accident occurred on 09-04-2024 at about 8.30 p.m, but the FIR was lodged on 13-04-2024 at about 11.00 a.m., and hence it is evident that the FIR is lodged after 5 days of occurrence of the accident.
Further on perusal of the contents of Ex.P3 & 5 spot mahazar and IMV report, the petitioner successfully established the negligence of rider of motor cycle bearing No. KA-64-W-1950 and thereby no reasons are made out to consider the contributory negligence by the petitioner as the petitioner is a pillion rider.
In a claim for compensation under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319 Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others.
20. As per well settled principle of law, the standard of proof in the claim petition like the present is preponderance of the probability.
There are no grounds to disbelieve the case of petitioner in the absence of rebuttal evidence.
All the materials available on record leading to show that, petitioner has sustained injuries in the accident took place on 09-04-2024 which is caused by the rider of the motor cycle bearing No.KA-64-W-1950 which belongs to respondent No.1 and insured with respondent No.2.
There is no reason to discard the evidence of petitioner.
In the claim petition like present one strict proof is not necessary, but preponderance of probabilities is sufficient.
At the time of alleged accident the petitioner was aged about 38 years.
No doubt that the PW.5 is not a treated doctor but assessed the disability of neurological assessment by using DGHS guidelines of Indian Phsyciatric association.
Nothing been elicited to disbelieve the case of the petitioner at the time of cross examination of PW.5.
But when the petitioner can answer the fact of accident in a proper and accurate way, whether the evidence of Pw.5 regarding the cognitive disability can be considered or not has to be looked into.
No doubt that the petitioner's normal life is disturbed by the accident.
But as per the evidence of PW.5 doctor in the complex situation the petitioner cannot behave normally.
As per the PW.5 the petitioner behaves normal in the simple comprehensive situation.
But in the complex situations the condition of the petitioner is impaired.
By considering the same, for a person to lead his life in a normal way without depending on others, they have to behave and react normally in both normal and complex situation.
